sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**
HCLTech reported a consolidated total income of ₹119.54 billion for the year ended 31 March 2025, representing a 7.3% increase from ₹111.41 billion in the previous year. The company's revenue from operations stood at ₹117.06 billion, with the IT and Business Services segment contributing ₹86.44 billion, followed by Engineering and R&D services at ₹18.96 billion, and HCL Software at ₹11.66 billion. Net profit for the year increased by 11.1% to ₹17.40 billion from ₹15.71 billion in the previous year.

**Investment Thesis**
Our investment thesis for HCLTech is positive, driven by the company's consistent revenue growth and improving profitability. With a segment result of ₹14.80 billion from the IT and Business Services segment, which accounts for approximately 69% of the company's total revenue, HCLTech demonstrates a strong presence in the IT services market. The company's ability to maintain a stable margin profile, with a profit before tax of ₹23.26 billion, despite increasing expenses, is a testament to its operational efficiency. While peer comparison is not possible due to the lack of available data, HCLTech's financial performance suggests a promising outlook for investors. We believe that the company's diversified revenue streams, coupled with its focus on digital transformation and innovation, position it well for long-term growth and sustainability.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body: HCLTech is a leading IT services company that has delivered industry-leading growth and maintained steady profitability despite uncertainty in the macro-economic and geopolitical environment. In FY25, the company reported a consolidated revenue of ₹117,055 crores, a growth of 6.5% from the preceding year. The company's business can be broadly segmented into three categories: IT and Business Services, Engineering and R&D services, and HCLSoftware. The IT and Business Services segment accounted for 73.8% of the total revenue, generating ₹86,438 crores in revenue, while the Engineering and R&D services segment accounted for 16.2% of the total revenue, generating ₹18,960 crores in revenue. The HCLSoftware segment accounted for 10.3% of the total revenue, generating ₹12,049 crores in revenue. The company's revenue is also diversified across geographies, with the United States of America (USA) and Europe being the dominant markets, accounting for 58.1% and 26.7% of the total revenue, respectively.

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet health of HCLTech appears robust, with a strong net worth position. As of 31 March 2025, the company's total equity stood at ₹68,271 crore, comprising share capital, reserves and surplus, and other comprehensive income. The retained earnings component of the equity was significant, at ₹67,720 crore, indicating a substantial accumulation of profits over the years. The cash flow hedging reserve, which is a part of other comprehensive income, was ₹357 crore, down from ₹497 crore in the previous year.

In terms of cash flow, HCLTech generated a net cash flow of ₹22,261 crore from operating activities for the year ended 31 March 2025, which was slightly lower than the ₹22,448 crore generated in the previous year. The company's cash flow from operations was supported by a profit before tax of ₹23,261 crore, adjusted for non-cash items such as depreciation and amortization expense of ₹4,084 crore. The net cash used in investing activities was ₹4,914 crore, primarily due to payments for business acquisitions and investments in securities. The net cash used in financing activities was ₹18,561 crore, mainly on account of dividend payments of ₹16,250 crore and repayment of borrowings. As a result, the company's cash and cash equivalents balance decreased to ₹8,245 crore as of 31 March 2025, from ₹9,441 crore in the previous year.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of HCLTech has expressed its commitment to delivering sustainable growth and shareholder value, positioning the company for continued success. As stated in the annual report, allocation decisions are made with a focus on growth, profitability, cash generation, return ratios, prudent use of capital, and strong governance. The company aims to deliver top-quartile Total Shareholder Return (TSR) and has a track record of outperforming its peers, with a cumulative TSR of 314.5% over 5 years. In FY25, HCLTech delivered industry-leading growth, with revenue of ₹117,055 crores, representing a 6.5% growth, and a net profit of ₹17,390 crores, which grew by 10.8%. The company's EBIT margin was 18.3%, with EBIT of ₹21,420 crores, up 7% from the previous year.

The management has also emphasized the importance of risk management, with a comprehensive approach to identifying, assessing, mitigating, and monitoring enterprise risks. The company's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework is based on the ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management standard and the COSO ERM Integrated Framework. The management has classified its risk universe into five principal categories: Strategic, Financial, Cyber and Resilience, Operational, and Governance and Compliance. With a strong focus on governance, risk management, and employee development, HCLTech has established itself as a leader in the Indian IT services industry, with a brand value of ₹8.9 billion (approximately ₹66.67 billion, using an approximate exchange rate), up 17% year-over-year. The company's commitment to investing in its people, with over 106,000 employees trained in AI/GenAI in FY25, has resulted in one of the lowest employee attrition rates in the industry and a stable leadership team.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The key risks associated with HCLTech's business are multifaceted and can be categorized into five principal areas: Strategic, Financial, Cyber and Resilience, Operational, and Governance and Compliance. Strategically, the company faces risks related to its business model, including the inability to keep up with changing client needs, attract quality talent, and adapt to evolving operating models. This is exacerbated by emerging technologies such as GenAI, which poses both a threat to the existing business model and an opportunity to offer new services. To mitigate these risks, HCLTech has developed a Strategic Risk & Opportunity Management (SROM) framework that helps identify risks and opportunities ahead of time. Additionally, the company recognizes the risks associated with portfolio concentration and has implemented diversification strategies to mitigate risk and propel growth.

In terms of specific business risks, HCLTech faces constraints on service delivery due to technological limitations, pandemics, geopolitical developments, and the lack of talent availability. The company has implemented measures to minimize these risks, including continuous monitoring of the global technology market, collaboration with advisors, clients, partners, and governments, and leveraging its Centers of Excellence (COEs), internal innovation platforms, and ecosystem partnerships. Furthermore, HCLTech has expanded its New Vistas (NV) and nearshore presence to access the best talent and develop service-delivery resilience. The company's top twenty clients contribute around 30% of its revenue, and it has about 950 clients each offering over ₹1 million (approximately ₹950 crore in total from these clients), which helps mitigate concentration risk. Overall, HCLTech's risk management framework is designed to identify, assess, mitigate, monitor, and report on enterprise risks that may impact its strategic and business objectives, while maintaining the highest standards of corporate governance.

sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
Recent Developments

HCLTech has been actively managing its strategic risks, including the threat posed by emerging technologies such as GenAI, which is seen as both a risk and an opportunity to offer new services. The company has developed a Strategic Risk & Opportunity Management (SROM) framework to identify and mitigate risks ahead of time. This framework has led to several key strategic initiatives across offerings, corporate functions, and geographic expansions. Additionally, HCLTech has been diversifying its portfolio to reduce concentration risk, with the top twenty clients contributing around 30% of its revenue. The company has also been expanding into new geographies, strengthening and diversifying its offerings, including its Software portfolio.

In terms of financial developments, HCLTech's cash flows from operating activities for the year ended 31 March 2025 were ₹22,261 crore, with a net cash flow used in investing activities of ₹4,914 crore and a net cash flow used in financing activities of ₹18,561 crore. The company's cash and cash equivalents at the end of the year were ₹8,245 crore. HCLTech has also been actively managing its financial risks, including credit risk, currency risk, and acquisition and integration risk. The company uses foreign exchange forward contracts and a combination of options to mitigate the risk of foreign currency fluctuations, and has a robust integration and performance management framework to ensure the effective integration of acquired businesses.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for HCLTech is supported by the company's industry-leading growth and steady profitability, with revenue reaching ₹117.055 billion in FY25, representing a 6.5% growth, and profit increasing by 10.8% to ₹17.39 billion. The company's ability to outperform its peers for the second consecutive year, its strong brand value of ₹640.23 billion (approximately $8.9 billion converted to ₹), and its recognition as the world's fastest-growing IT services brand, all contribute to a positive outlook. Additionally, HCLTech's focus on investing in employee upskilling, particularly in AI and GenAI, with over 106,000 employees trained in FY25, and its low employee attrition rates, position the company for continued success.

The bear case, on the other hand, is centered around the risks associated with HCLTech's business model, including the potential inability to keep up with changing client needs and the threat posed by emerging technologies such as GenAI. The company's concentration in certain business segments, industry sectors, and geographic regions also poses a risk, although HCLTech has taken steps to mitigate this through diversification and expansion into new geographies and offerings. The base case assumes that HCLTech will continue to deliver steady growth and profitability, driven by its strong portfolio, client relationships, and investments in employee upskilling, while navigating the risks associated with its business model and the rapidly evolving technology landscape. With a return on invested capital (ROIC) of 37.9% and an operating cash flow to net income conversion of 129%, HCLTech is well-positioned to continue delivering top-quartile total shareholder return (TSR).

Strategic Risks Primary Risk Details Mitigation Business Model HCLTech operates in a fast-paced industry. An inability to keep up with changing client needs, attract quality talent and adapt to evolving operating models can affect business growth. Moreover, emerging technologies such as GenAI pose a threat to the existing business model and an opportunity to offer new services. • Our strategy office has developed a Strategic Risk & Opportunity Management (SROM) framework that helps to scan signals and identify risks and opportunities ahead of time. Such signals are evaluated for their strength, scope of impact, time horizon to impact etc. and are then planned through a strategic planning process and enabled for execution. Over the past few years, several key strategic initiatives across offerings, corporate functions, geo expansions, etc., have emanated from this framework. Portfolio Concentration HCLTech recognizes the risks associated with being concentrated in certain business segments, industry sectors and geographic regions. Any negative event impacting these areas could have a material impact on the company’s performance. • As a best practice, we assess our portfolio for concentration risk at regular intervals on various dimensions. We use diversification as one of the key tools to mitigate risk and propel growth. Our recent geographic, vertical and client market expansions have been driven by this approach. • We try to maintain a healthy balance and avoid over- dependency across dimensions like verticals, clients, geographies and business segments. For example, our client base and revenue share across verticals are well spread. Top twenty clients contribute around 30% of our revenue and we have about 950 clients each offering over $1M. Many of these clients are G2000 or equivalent, giving us the opportunity to expand wallet share and mitigate concentration risk. We have reduced regional dependency by expanding into new geographies and have strategically strengthened and diversified our offerings, including our Software portfolio. Business Delivery HCLTech faces risks from constraints on service delivery due to technological limitations, pandemics, geopolitical developments and the lack of talent availability. Any of these factors can adversely impact the company. • HCLTech continuously monitors the global technology market and collaborates closely with advisors, clients, partners and governments to minimize risk related to its delivery model. • We leverage our COEs, internal innovation platforms, subject matter experts, practice teams and ecosystem partnerships to overcome technology-related delivery challenges. • We continue to expand our New Vistas (NV) and nearshore presence to access the best talent and develop service-delivery resilience. 87 HCLTech Annual Report 2024-25

eval_context.content: Financial Risks Primary Risk Details Mitigation Default or Credit HCLTech’s credit risk is concentrated in cash and bank balances, intercorporate deposits, customer receivables, finance lease receivables, investment securities and derivative instruments. All financial instruments mentioned above carry a risk of nonperformance by counterparties. • During the pre-contracting stage of the sales cycle, HCLTech assesses the clients’ credit rating and financial reliability when investments or extended payment terms are involved. In the post-contracting stage, we continuously monitor our clients’ resilience by tracking and analyzing their financial reliability, financial performance, published credit ratings, economic trends, historical debts and customer receivables. This continuous monitoring process significantly helps mitigate credit risks for the company. Currency HCLTech generates most of its revenue from clients outside of India and receives payments primarily in foreign currencies. The company’s clients are primarily corporations based in the US, Europe and other geos and its receivables are concentrated here. Similarly, as HCLTech has delivery teams based in various countries, most of its costs are also denominated in foreign currencies. This situation puts HCLTech at risk of economic loss due to changes in exchange rates. • HCLTech uses foreign exchange forward contracts and a combination of options to mitigate the risk of foreign currency fluctuations on its net receivables/payables and forecasted transactions in certain currencies. • The company’s Board establishes prudent governing policies and processes that determine the duration of hedges, the percentage of risk to be covered and the counterparty risk to be assumed. Acquisition and Integration HCLTech makes strategic acquisitions on an ongoing basis. The success of these acquisitions hinge on effective integration and synergy realization. Internal factors, as well as external factors beyond our control, can also play a role. These factors may include the risk of impairing goodwill, failed synergies and other intangibles if integration is not managed effectively. Additionally, a lack of integration process can limit the ability to capture synergy benefits. • Our governance program includes a robust mechanism to ensure regular reviews at multiple stages, starting from the deal stage to integration, with participation from Line of Business leadership to Executive Management to the Board of Directors, to address issues effectively. • HCLTech’s robust integration and performance management framework enables the acquired businesses and HCLTech to achieve the acquisition objectives. Our Integration and Performance Management Office (IPMO) manages the integration process and ensures value creation.

All financial instruments mentioned above carry a risk of nonperformance by counterparties. • During the pre-contracting stage of the sales cycle, HCLTech assesses the clients’ credit rating and financial reliability when investments or extended payment terms are involved. In the post-contracting stage, we continuously monitor our clients’ resilience by tracking and analyzing their financial reliability, financial performance, published credit ratings, economic trends, historical debts and customer receivables. This continuous monitoring process significantly helps mitigate credit risks for the company. Currency HCLTech generates most of its revenue from clients outside of India and receives payments primarily in foreign currencies. The company’s clients are primarily corporations based in the US, Europe and other geos and its receivables are concentrated here. Similarly, as HCLTech has delivery teams based in various countries, most of its costs are also denominated in foreign currencies. This situation puts HCLTech at risk of economic loss due to changes in exchange rates. • HCLTech uses foreign exchange forward contracts and a combination of options to mitigate the risk of foreign currency fluctuations on its net receivables/payables and forecasted transactions in certain currencies. • The company’s Board establishes prudent governing policies and processes that determine the duration of hedges, the percentage of risk to be covered and the counterparty risk to be assumed. Acquisition and Integration HCLTech makes strategic acquisitions on an ongoing basis. The success of these acquisitions hinge on effective integration and synergy realization. Internal factors, as well as external factors beyond our control, can also play a role. These factors may include the risk of impairing goodwill, failed synergies and other intangibles if integration is not managed effectively. Additionally, a lack of integration process can limit the ability to capture synergy benefits. • Our governance program includes a robust mechanism to ensure regular reviews at multiple stages, starting from the deal stage to integration, with participation from Line of Business leadership to Executive Management to the Board of Directors, to address issues effectively. • HCLTech’s robust integration and performance management framework enables the acquired businesses and HCLTech to achieve the acquisition objectives. Our Integration and Performance Management Office (IPMO) manages the integration process and ensures value creation.

Primary Risk Details Mitigation Tax HCLTech is subject to taxes in several jurisdictions worldwide and benefits from tax advantages in India and other countries. Changes to tax laws in India and other countries where HCLTech has a significant presence could impact the company’s effective tax rate. As HCLTech operates in multiple jurisdictions, transfer pricing arrangements among legal entities in these regions are subject to review by various tax authorities. • HCLTech employs specialized tax teams that keep abreast of the latest tax developments in different countries, seek advice and support from external professional firms/consultants/lawyers and implement appropriate tax planning strategies based on changes in tax laws. • To mitigate tax risks associated with transfer pricing, we have established advance pricing agreements in several countries and periodically review them with external consultants. Primary Risk Details Mitigation Talent Management and Development Managing talent and meeting the ever-increasing demand for talent poses a significant ongoing risk to HCLTech. We face the risk of failing to fulfill resource demands due to a talent shortage, which could negatively impact top-line growth and organizational expansion. Furthermore, the risk of higher attrition rates could equally affect delivery capability and growth plans. Additionally, legislative changes restricting work visa availability and deglobalization could have a further impact. • HCLTech has developed a robust process for hiring and making talent productive worldwide. Our comprehensive training strategy is designed to meet the needs and goals of all employees, encompassing professional, technical, functional and leadership development. This approach is crucial for mitigating the risk of an unprepared leadership pipeline due to insufficient development and succession planning. • We have implemented various initiatives to attract, engage and retain a stable, content and diverse multi-generational employee pool. • To mitigate the potential effects of legislative actions, we have thoughtfully reduced our reliance on work visas by recruiting more local talent. This approach has led to one of the industry’s highest local talent ratios. Furthermore, leveraging nearshore centers and focusing on onshore delivery has minimized our dependency on work visas. Business Highlights In FY25, HCLTech demonstrated resilience and growth supported by its diverse and all-weather portfolio despite uncertainty in the global economy and geopolitics. HCLTech reported a consolidated revenue of $13.8 billion in FY25, an increase of 4.7% from the preceding year in constant currency (CC). The growth is attributed to our strategic emphasis on differentiated offerings, robust client relationships, adaptability to market conditions and ability to seize emerging opportunities. Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT) for the fiscal year was at 18.3%, an improvement of 7 basis points (bps) year-over-year (YoY). The net income was at $2.0 billion, a 7.6% increase YoY and the net income margin was 14.7%. Our Operating Cash Flow (OCF) and Free Cash Flow (FCF) were $2.6 billion and $2.5 billion, respectively. The Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) was 37.9%, up 411 bps YoY. Our client base grew considerably across various revenue categories in FY25. HCLTech received several global recognitions in FY25, the most notable being recognized as the No. 1 India- headquartered company in TIME magazine’s list of World’s Best Companies 2024 and one of America’s Most Reliable Companies 2025 by Newsweek. Our innovative technology services and software portfolio garnered over 400 leadership positions in analyst recognitions and we were the only service provider to be rated Customers’ Choice in 4 out of 5 Gartner Peer Insights Voice of the Customer (VoC) reports across IT services markets (as of April 2025). Brand Finance declared us the world’s fastest-growing IT Services brand in 2025, with our brand value increasing by 17% YoY to $8.9 billion. HCLTech was named a Top Employer by the Top Employers Institute for the third consecutive year, achieving top honors in North America, APAC and Europe. Forbes recognized us as one of the World’s Best Employers for the fifth year in a row, making us the only India-headquartered company in the professional services category to consistently rank among the global top ten. Sustainability remains at the core of our operations, as evidenced by our Gold Status from EcoVadis and recognition as one of Ethisphere’s 2025 World’s Most Ethical Companies for the second consecutive year. HCLFoundation continues to drive meaningful social change, impacting over 7.5 million lives in India. In the Institutional Investor Research Annual Asia Executive Team Survey, HCLTech was the most decorated India-headquartered IT services company, achieving the No. 1 ranking in twenty-one categories within the Technology IT Services & Software sector. In FY25, we also celebrated the 25th anniversary of our Initial Public Offering (IPO). We grew significantly during periods of high discretionary spending as well as during times when spending softened during the last 25 years.
